Subject: Dedicated renewal + mid-term GPU uplift questions

Hi Priya,

Hope you had a good break. Our Dedicated contract with Redwood is up for renewal in late Feb and early Q2 we'll likely need to add capacity for a new recommendation workload. Before we start the formal procurement loop I wanted to align on a few items so we can scope the RFP:  

1) Pricing model options: for a mid-term uplift, do you do prorated monthly add-ons to an existing commit or do you require a contract amendment with a new baseline commit? What are the discount tiers for incremental GPU vRAM capacity?

2) Throughput guarantees: we need a 99th percentile token latency SLA for interactive workloads (max 250ms for 1–2k token responses). Is that tied to pool sizing, and what are the measurement windows?

3) Fallback and credit policy: if you fail to meet latency SLOs due to capacity events, what credits or fallback model do you offer — e.g., bursting to public pool with a reimbursement structure?

If you can share a few example commercial structures and a term sheet stub, that would help us engage procurement. We are also happy to schedule a 30-min sync with your sales/solutions team.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben from Sales who handles commercial structuring and Tessa on our delivery side for SLA/ops detail. High level answers below, and we can put formal terms in a short term sheet.

1) Mid-term uplifts: two common approaches — (A) additive top-up to the existing commit with prorated billing and the same effective discount ladder for the added units, or (B) a contract amendment that resets baseline commit (typically used when uplift exceeds ~30% of existing commit). We recommend top-up for <30% growth; beyond that, an amendment gives better unit economics.

2) Throughput & latency SLAs: our 99th percentile token latency SLOs are tied to a combination of pool size, instance class, and configured batching/kv-cache settings. Measurement windows are rolling 30-day for SLOs, and we publish per-route dashboards in Console. For your target (<=250ms p99 at 1–2k tokens) we usually size to N+20% headroom on your peak qps profile and include reserved burst capacity.

3) Fallback/credits: standard is an operational fallback policy — automatic routing to compatible model variants (same family, lower mem) and cross-region failover. Credits are available for SLA violations per contract: a % of monthly commit applied as a credit (tiered by severity/recurrence). We can also include a temporary burst-to-hosted option with discounted bill-back in exceptional outages.

Ben will follow up with 2–3 commercial options and a short term sheet for procurement. Tessa, can you prepare a quick sizing note that maps their 95th/99th latency target to pool options?

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Director, Commercial Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — quick note with three commercial structures attached (term sheet stub). Summary below:  

Option A — Top-up (recommended for <30% uplift):
- Additive monthly billing for extra GPUs; prorated in the current billing cycle.
- Same discount tier as existing commit until new total crosses next tier.
- No minimum extension to contract term.

Option B — Amended baseline (recommended for >=30% uplift):
- Reset baseline commit, 12–24 month term required for mid-size uplifts.
- Better unit price: additional 10–18% discount on incremental units depending on term length.

Option C — Flex reserve (commit + buffer):
- Maintain current baseline, purchase a smaller guaranteed commit plus a burst pool.
- Lower committed spend, higher overage rate but with predictable burst credits.

Throughput guarantee add-on (optional):
- +1.5% of monthly commit as a service uplift for a measured p99 latency SLA with >99.9% availability. Includes monthly reporting and 30-day remediation windows.

I've attached a term sheet stub and a Q4 throughput metrics CSV you can share with procurement. If you'd like, we can price each option against your current commit. Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk options?

Hi Elena — putting some technical context behind the examples Ben will send. Short answers:  

- p99 measurement: per-route by default (Console exposes per-route p99 and per-model metrics). You can elect to use an aggregated cross-route p99 for contractual SLOs but pricing reflects the extra instrumentation and aggregation.

- Outage definition: a sustained inability to serve >5 minutes on the route at configured capacity, or a p99 breach >15% above target for a rolling 1-hour window after deduplication of transient spikes. Credits escalate with recurrence.

- VPC/private control-plane: no mandatory price delta for VPC itself, but on-prem or air-gapped deployments are licensed differently. Data retention in your VPC (90 days) is supported — we'll need a short ops addendum outlining storage endpoints and access patterns. That addendum does not materially change per-GPU pricing but may add a one-time provisioning fee.

Ben — can you attach the worked example (12m vs 24m) with the numbers mapped to Options A/B/C and include the SLA add-on as a separate line item?

Thanks,
Tessa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
